description: An eight by eight grid of stereo loops, one track per column, that records and launches takes on the beats of a NINJAM jam clock

params.text: Press it empty to start recording on the next beat, filled to launch it, playing to stop it; press it while recording to close the take on the next beat and loop it, or press again to keep recording
Launches every filled cell in its row and stops the track under every empty one, on the next beat; the last scene pressed wins
Stops whatever that track is playing, and throws away a recording in progress on it
Stops every track, and throws away any recording in progress
Puts that track's incoming audio on air, green feeding it into MIX for the room, cyan keeping it private by routing it to CUE instead
Latches overdub on, so the selected playing cell keeps layering what comes in each time round until it is switched off

inputs.text: The left channel of that track's own input; patching it makes the track take its audio from its own pair of jacks rather than from INS
The right channel of that track's own input; with nothing patched, the track's left jack feeds both sides
Feeds all eight tracks down one poly cable, channels 1 and 2 going to track 1, channels 3 and 4 to track 2 and so on; a track whose own left jack is patched takes that instead of its pair here

outputs.text: The left side of the submix of the tracks that are on air; patch it to a Ninjam module's left input to transmit it
The right side of the submix of the tracks that are on air; patch it to a Ninjam module's right input to transmit it
The left side of the private monitor mix, carrying the tracks whose transmit latch is off
The right side of the private monitor mix, carrying the tracks whose transmit latch is off
Carries the eight tracks down one poly cable, channels 1 and 2 for track 1, channels 3 and 4 for track 2 and so on

notes: Placed immediately beside a Ninjam module, on either side, it takes that room's tempo and interval; standing alone it runs on a simulated interval whose length is set in the menu
A press does not act at once: it is queued, shown by a blinking outline, and commits on the next beat. One queued press per track, and the last press wins
A launched take cycles at the length and speed it was recorded at, so a tempo change on the server leaves it running as it was; only queued presses and a recording in flight are cancelled
A recording caps at one interval. Carry on playing and the take chains into the next empty cell down the column until an interval comes in quiet; the chain then replays from its first cell
Click a track's name strip to rename it, up to four characters. With a MindMeld MixMaster feeding INS the names copy between the two on their own
Every committed take is written as an OGG file under the jam folder, and the grid comes back with the patch
Nothing reaches a NINJAM room by itself: patch MIX into a Ninjam module's input jacks to transmit the submix
menu: Simulated interval (when no Ninjam clock) — sets the interval the grid runs at when no Ninjam module is beside it, from 2 seconds up to 32 seconds
New clips: repeats — sets how many times a newly recorded take plays before it stops, the infinity choice leaving it cycling
New clips: decay per repetition — sets how far a newly recorded take drops in level each time round, down to -6dB
Capture: auto-advance while playing — when off, a recording that runs past the end of the interval stops there instead of chaining into the next empty cell down the column
Clear all slots — empties every cell in the grid
Choose folder… — picks the folder the recorded takes are written to
Reset to ~/Music/jams — puts the take folder back to the default
Open this session's folder — opens the folder holding this session's takes
New session (keep loops) — starts a fresh session folder and leaves the takes in the grid
New session (clear grid) — starts a fresh session folder and empties the grid
Embed takes in patch — when on, the recorded audio is stored inside the patch file, so a shared patch carries its loops with it
Repeats — on a grid cell's own right-click menu: how many times that take plays before it stops
Decay per repetition — on a grid cell's own right-click menu: how far that take drops in level each time round
After — on a grid cell's own right-click menu: whether that take stops when it is done, or launches a numbered slot in the same track
Clear slot — on a grid cell's own right-click menu: empties that cell
Reset to default — on a track name's own right-click menu: puts that track's name back to its default
